The XML direction has two uses beyond code generation: build an .xlsx directly from XML a transform engine (e.g. XSLT) already produces, no code required; or convert an existing .xlsx to XML for text-based diffing and version control in systems like git, with deterministically ordered output so real content changes stay isolated in the diff. The XML/JSON directions each have two uses beyond code generation: build an .xlsx directly from XML/JSON a transform engine (e.g. XSLT) or generation script already produces, no code required; or convert an existing .xlsx to XML/JSON for text-based diffing and version control in systems like git, with deterministically ordered output so real content changes stay isolated in the diff.
